contentText:
The Federal Communications Commission voted unanimously to allow state and local prisons to jam cellphones. In an announcement on Thursday , the FCC argues the rule will help combat an "influx of contraband cellphones" used to carry out crimes from prison.

Jammers are generally banned under Section 333 of the Communications Act of 1934 , though they're used at some federal facilities. FCC Chair Brendan Carr claims that giving correctional facilities access to this technology will help prevent prisoners from using phones for illegal activity.
